primary.key: The Gods seek him who presses out the Soma; they desire not sleep They punish sloth unweariedly.
primary.s: Amid the Kanvas’ call to Indra, the hymn turns to the gods and the worshipper; Sāyaṇa, on 8.2.18, reads it as the gods, wishing to guard the presser, keeping him ever awake, and takes the word rendered ‘sloth’ as the gladdening Soma they tirelessly reach.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.2.18, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.२, revision 302478 (2021)

basis.words: "सुन्वन्तं सोमाभिषवं कुर्वन्तं यजमानं "देवाः इन्द्रादयः सर्वे "इच्छन्ति रक्षितुम् । “स्वप्नाय “न “स्पृहयन्ति । स्वप्नावस्थां तस्य सुन्वतो नेप्सन्ति । सर्वदा प्रबुद्धमेव कुर्वन्तीत्यर्थः । … यत एवमतः कारणात् “अतन्द्राः अनलसा देवाः “प्रमादं प्रकर्षेण मदकरं तदीयं सोमं “यन्ति प्राप्नुवन्ति
basis.gloss: All the gods, Indra and the rest, wish to protect the sacrificer who presses the Soma. They do not desire sleep: they do not want the state of sleep for that presser; the sense is that they keep him always awake. … Because this is so, the unwearied, unslothful gods reach pramāda, that is, his Soma, which gladdens exceedingly.

standby.key: With might hath Indra spread out heaven and earth, with power hath Indra lighted up the Sun.
standby.s: After calling Indra to rite and battle alike, the hymn praises his works across the worlds; Sāyaṇa, on 8.3.6, takes the lighting of the Sun as Indra freeing it from Svarbhānu, the asura who had covered it, by slaying him.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.3.6, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.३, revision 354994 (2022)

basis.words: अयम् “इन्द्रः “शवः शवस आत्मीयस्य बलस्य “मह्ना महिम्ना महत्त्वेन “रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ "पप्रथत् अप्रथयत् विस्तारितवान् । तथा स्वर्भानुनावृतं "सूर्यम् अयमेव “इन्द्रः “अरोचयत् अदीपयत्। तस्यासुरस्य वधेन प्रकाशितवान् ।
basis.gloss: This Indra, by the greatness of his own strength, spread out heaven and earth. Likewise this very Indra made shine the sun that Svarbhānu had covered: he brought it to light by slaying that asura.

primary.key: There where the mountains downward slope, there by the meeting of the streams The Sage was manifest with song.
primary.s: Amid long praise of Indra’s might, the hymn tells where a sage appears; Sāyaṇa, on 8.6.28, takes the sage as Indra, manifest through the rite or praise offered among hills and river meetings, and infers that the singers too worship in such places.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.6.28, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.६, revision 314241 (2021)

basis.words: “गिरीणां पर्वतानाम् “उपह्वरे उपह्वर्तव्ये प्रान्ते “नदीनां सरितां “संगथे संगमने “च ईदृग्विधे देशे क्रियमाणया “धिया यागक्रियया स्तुत्या वा “विप्रः मेधावीन्द्रः “अजायत प्रादुर्भवति । अतो वयमपि तादृशे देशे यजामः स्तुमो वेति भावः ।
basis.gloss: On the slopes of the mountains and at the confluence of the rivers, by the thought, that is the rite of sacrifice or the praise, performed in such a place, the wise one, Indra, becomes manifest. Hence we too sacrifice or praise in such a place: that is the sense.

standby.key: Neither the heavens nor firmaments nor regions of the earth contain Indra, the Thunderer with his might.
standby.s: After Indra’s blows against Vrtra and the Dasyu Susna, the hymn sets his might against the worlds; Sāyaṇa, on 8.6.15, reads it as his strength exceeding even the heavens, and, citing a Brāhmaṇa, counts each of the three worlds as threefold.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.6.15, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.६, revision 314241 (2021)

basis.words: “द्यावः द्युलोका इमम् “इन्द्रम् “ओजसा बलेन “न “विव्यचन्त न व्याप्नुवन्ति । द्युलोकेभ्योऽप्यस्य बलमधिकमित्यर्थः । … त्रयो वा इमे त्रिवृतो लोकाः' (ऐ. आ. १. १. २ ) इति ब्राह्मणादेकैकस्य लोकस्य त्रित्वम् । ‘तिस्रो भूमीः' (ऋ. सं. २. २७.८) इत्यादिनिगमाच्च
basis.gloss: The heavens do not encompass this Indra in strength: the sense is that his strength is greater even than the heavens. … From the Brāhmaṇa text ‘these worlds are three, each threefold’ (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 1.1.2), each single world is threefold; and also from Vedic texts such as ‘three earths’ (Rig Veda 2.27.8).

primary.key: Three places of the Asvins, erst concealed, are made apparent now.
primary.s: Closing a long summons of the Asvins to the Kanvas’ Soma, the hymn turns to their approach; Sāyaṇa, on 8.8.23, takes the three places as the three wheels of their chariot, hidden until now, citing another hymn for its three wheels.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.8.23, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.८, revision 208919 (2019)

basis.words: “त्रीणि त्रिसंख्याकानि अनयोः “अश्विनोः देवयो रथस्य संबन्धीनि “पदानि चक्राणि “गुहा गुहायां वर्तमानान्येतावन्तं कालमदृश्यमानानि “परः गुहायाः परस्ताद्दृष्टिगोचरे देशे “आविः “सन्ति आविर्भवन्ति ॥ … आश्विनस्य रथस्य चक्रत्रयोपेतत्वं च रथस्त्रिचक्रः परि वर्तते ' (ऋ. सं. ४. ३६. १ ) इत्यादिनिगमान्तरे प्रसिद्धम् ।
basis.gloss: The three ‘places’ belonging to the chariot of these two gods, the Asvins, are its wheels: lying in a hidden place, unseen until this time, they now appear beyond the hiding place, in a region within sight. … That the Asvins’ chariot has three wheels is well known from other Vedic texts, such as ‘the three-wheeled chariot goes round’ (Rig Veda 4.36.1).

standby.key: When Visnu, through thine energy, strode wide those three great steps of his, Then thy two beautiful Bay Steeds carried thee on.
standby.s: In three verses sharing a refrain on Indra’s Bay Steeds, the hymn recalls his great moments; Sāyaṇa, on 8.12.27, takes Visnu as Indra’s younger brother, the pervading god, whose three steps strode over and measured out the three worlds.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.12.27, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.१२, revision 190547 (2019)

basis.words: हे इन्द्र “ते तवानुजः “विष्णुः व्यापनशीलो देवः “ओजसा बलेन “यदा यस्मिन् काले “त्रीणि पदानि पदत्रयरूपेण त्रीँल्लोकान् “विचक्रमे विक्रान्तवान् परिच्छिन्नवान् । गतमन्यत् ॥
basis.gloss: O Indra, when your younger brother Visnu, the god whose nature is to pervade, by his strength strode the three worlds in the form of three steps, stepped across them and measured them out. The rest has been explained.

primary.key: And as we human beings, O Adityas, are akin to death, Graciously lengthen ye our lives that we may live.
primary.s: Ending a hymn asking the Adityas for shelter and release from sin, the singers plead for life; Sāyaṇa, on 8.18.22, takes kinship with death as kinship with Yama, their death being near, and reads the plea as for long continuance in life.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.18.22, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.१८, revision 327230 (2021)

basis.words: हे "आदित्याः “ये “चित् ये च वयं “मनवः मनुष्याः “हि यस्मात् “मृत्युबन्धवः “स्मसि मृत्योर्यमस्य बन्धुभूताः प्रत्यासन्नमरणा भवामः अतो हेतोस्तेषां “नः अस्माकं “जीवसे जीवनाय चिरकालावस्थानाय "आयुः जीवितं “सु “प्र “तिरेतन शोभनं प्रवर्धयत
basis.gloss: O Adityas, since we men are kinsmen of Death, that is of Yama, we whose death is near: for that reason, for our living, for our continuing a long time, prolong our life well.

standby.key: IF I, O Indra, were, like thee, the single Sovran of all wealth, My worshipper should be rich in kine.
standby.s: Opening a hymn that praises Indra’s gifts and his victories over Vala and Namuci, the singer begins with a wish; Sāyaṇa, on 8.14.1, takes its drift to be that one who praises Indra, the lord of wealth, could hardly fail to own cattle.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.14.1, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.१४, revision 353462 (2022)

basis.words: हे “इन्द्र “यथा “त्वम् “एक “इत् एक एव केवलं “वस्वः वसुनः धनस्य ईंशिषे एवम् “अहम् अपि यत् यदि “ईशीय ऐश्वर्ययुक्तः स्यां तदानीं “मे मम "स्तोता “गोसखा स्यात् गोभिः सहितो भवेत् । ईश्वरस्य तव स्तोता कुतो हेतोर्गोसहितो न भवेत् अपि तु भवेदित्यभिप्रायः ॥
basis.gloss: O Indra, as you alone are sole lord of wealth, so if I too were lord, then my praiser would be possessed of cattle. For what reason should the praiser of you, the lord, not be possessed of cattle? Rather, he should be: that is the intent.

primary.key: Like a son cherished in his father’s house, Let our oblation rise unto the Gods.
primary.s: After the singer imagines trading places with Agni, the hymn returns to the offering; Sāyaṇa, on 8.19.27, takes the cherished son as Agni, fed with offerings like a son by his father, who carries the oblation to the gods from the house of sacrifice.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.19.27, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.१९, revision 402086 (2024)

basis.words: “पितुर्न “पुत्रः पितुः पुत्र इवास्माकं “सुभृतः सुष्ठु भर्ता । यद्वा । पित्रा पुत्र इवास्माभिः सम्यग्भृतो हविर्भिः पोषितः । अयमग्निः पुत्र इवास्माकं सुभृतः “दुरोणे यज्ञगृहे “देवान् “आ अभिलक्ष्य “नः अस्माकं "हविः “प्र “एतु प्र गमयतु ।
basis.gloss: Like a son of a father, our good supporter; or else, well borne by us as a son by a father, nourished with oblations. This Agni, cherished by us like a son, in the house, that is the house of sacrifice, towards the gods: let him convey our oblation forth.

standby.key: Thou findest not the wealthy man to be thy friend: those scorn thee who are flown with wine.
standby.s: Pleading as kinless singers for Indra’s friendship and gifts, the hymn turns to the rich and the drunken; Sāyaṇa, on 8.21.14, takes the rich man as one merely rich, who neither gives nor sacrifices, and the drunken as heedless men who harm Indra.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.21.14, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.२१, revision 398898 (2023)

basis.words: हे इन्द्र “रेवन्तं धनवन्तं केवलधनवन्तं दानादिरहितमयष्टारमाढ्यं मानवं “सख्याय सखिभावाय “नकिः “विन्दसे न भजसे नाश्रयसीत्यर्थः । अयष्टारो जनाः किं सन्तीत्यत आह । “सुराश्वः । … सुरया वृद्धास्तद्वत् प्रमत्ता नास्तिकाः “ते त्वां “पीयन्ति । पीयतिर्हिंसाकर्मा । हिंसन्ति । तान्नाश्रयसीत्यर्थः ॥
basis.gloss: O Indra, the rich man, merely rich, without giving and the like, a wealthy man who does not sacrifice: you do not take him into friendship; the sense is that you do not resort to him. To the question, what are the people who do not sacrifice, it says: ‘surāśvaḥ’ … swollen with surā and so heedless, unbelievers: they ‘pīyanti’ you; pīyati means to harm; they harm you. The sense is that you do not resort to them.

primary.key: Pathfinders even better than the eye, with unobstructed sight, Even when they close their lids, observant, they perceive.
primary.s: Praising Mitra and Varuna, who look down from the sky, the hymn turns to their sight; Sāyaṇa, on 8.25.9, takes the closing of lids as their waking every creature to its work, their gaze a mild light pervading day and night.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.25.9, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.२५, revision 201711 (2019)

basis.words: “अक्ष्णश्चित् चक्षुषोऽपि पूर्वं "गातुवित्तरा गातुवित्तरावतिशयेन मार्गवेत्तारौ । … मित्रावरुणौ । कीदृशौ। "नि "मिषन्ता निमिषन्तौ सर्वमुन्मेषयन्तौ स्वस्वकर्मणि "निचिरा नितरां चिरंतनौ तौ “अनुल्बणेन । उल्बणमिति दुःसहमग्नेस्तेजः । तद्वददुःसहेन "चक्षसा अहोरात्रयोर्व्याप्तेन तेजसैब "नि "चिक्यतुः पूजितौ बभूवतुः ।
basis.gloss: Even before the eye, knowers of the way in the highest degree … Mitra and Varuna. Of what kind? ‘Nimiṣantā’: causing all to open their eyes, each to its own work; very ancient; with a ‘not ulbaṇa’ gaze (ulbaṇa is the unbearable blaze of fire), a gaze not unbearable like that, a light pervading day and night: so they have been worshipped.

standby.key: As welcome guest of human kind, as offspring of the forest kings, The sages worship ancient Agni for his aid.
standby.s: After calling on Vyasva’s son to sing, the hymn tells how sages approach Agni; Sāyaṇa, on 8.23.25, explains Agni as offspring of the trees because he is born from the kindling sticks made of them, and takes the aid as protection of the rite.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.23.25, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.२३, revision 400837 (2024)

basis.words: “विप्राः मेधाविनो यजमानाः “मानुषाणां मनुष्याणाम् “अतिथिम् अतिथिवत्पूज्यं “वनस्पतीनां “सूनुं वनस्पतिरूपाभिररणीभिर्जायमानत्वेन तेषां सूनुं “प्रत्नं पुरातनमेवंविधम् “अग्निमवसे कर्मरक्षणाय “ईळते स्तुतिभिः स्तुवन्ति ॥
basis.gloss: The wise, the sacrificers, praise with hymns Agni, the guest of men, to be honoured like a guest; the son of the forest lords, their son because he is born from the kindling sticks, which have the form of trees; ancient; for ‘aid’, that is, for the protection of the rite.
